nodes.description: Contract owner address; set to msg.sender in constructor and used as access-control anchor and fee recipient.
Mapping of player address to withdrawable balance; credited in userChallenge and drained in userWithdraw.
Fixed array of six leader addresses holding the current champions of each tier.
Fixed array of six buy-in amounts (20/60/100/200/600/1000 finney) for each leader tier.
Caller-controlled address; used for ownership checks, balance keys, leader replacement and randomness.
Deployment constructor: sets owner and initializes leaders and buyins arrays.
View function returning balances[player] for an arbitrary address.
View function returning the current leaders array.
Owner-only function that swaps a leader slot, guarded by msg.sender == owner and leaders[index] == owner.
Withdraws the caller's full balance and forwards it with msg.sender.transfer.
Payable challenge function: requires msg.value == buyins[index], computes pseudo-random outcome and updates balances/leaders.
Local variable caching balances[msg.sender] before it is zeroed and transferred.
Tier index parameter selecting a leader/buyin slot; masked by require(index >= 0 && index < 6).
New leader address parameter written into leaders[index] by ownerChange.
Address parameter used as the lookup key into balances in publicGetBalance.
External ether transfer msg.sender.transfer(amount) after balance zeroing; classic reentrancy sink.
Unchecked additions/multiplications on balances in userChallenge (balances[...] += buyins[index], buyins[index] * 95 / 100).
Pseudo-random draw from blockhash(block.number - 1), leader address and msg.sender, which is predictable/manipulable.
Local variable holding the 1..100 draw used to decide the challenge outcome.

edges.reason: Constructor assigns owner = msg.sender during initialization.
Caller address msg.sender becomes the privileged owner in the constructor.
Constructor seeds all six leaders slots with the owner address.
Constructor fixes the buyin amounts for every tier.
publicGetBalance consumes the player parameter as a lookup key.
balances[player] is read and returned by publicGetBalance.
publicGetState returns the leaders array.
ownerChange authenticates with the caller-controlled msg.sender.
require(msg.sender == owner) gates the state mutation in ownerChange.
ownerChange reads and rewrites a leaders slot.
index parameter selects which leaders slot ownerChange modifies.
holder parameter is written into leaders[index].
userWithdraw keys the balances mapping with msg.sender.
userWithdraw zeroes balances[msg.sender] before paying out.
amount local copies the stored balance before it is cleared.
userWithdraw reaches the external ether transfer sink.
The transferred value derives from the stored balance amount.
transfer forwards ether/gas to msg.sender, allowing re-entry into userWithdraw (and userChallenge).
userChallenge validates msg.value against buyins[index].
index parameter selects the leader/buyin tier in userChallenge.
userChallenge reads and can overwrite leaders[index].
userChallenge executes unchecked balance additions and percentage math.
Balances credits from buyins[index] can overflow unchecked in Solidity 0.4.x.
The predictable random value controls which branch and payout userChallenge takes.
msg.sender feeds the randomness computation, letting the caller influence the draw.
userChallenge derives its outcome from blockhash/block state, a miner/challenger-influenceable source.
Local random is assigned from the weak randomness expression.

normalization_plan.reason: amount is a temporary holder of the payout value and exists only to feed msg.sender.transfer, so it collapses into the transfer unsafe_operation.
index is a tier selector consumed directly by userChallenge's require and array accesses; it folds into that core function.
holder is a pure argument written into leaders only through ownerChange and has no independent semantics.
player is used solely as the balances lookup key inside publicGetBalance.
random is the local result of the weak randomness expression and carries no meaning beyond that unsafe source.
